items.headline: Israel's security cabinet meets today for the first time since Oct 4 — the open question is whether the caretaker government can order a strike on Iran; Eisenkot, mandated to form the next government, warned Netanyahu against security moves during the transition (JFeed, Nov 13).

Oil: no fresh weekend escalation reported — Brent $95.84 / WTI $88.56 Fri settles, both -2.5% on the week and a second straight weekly loss; futures reopen tonight and weekend Iran/Saudi news is the first tape (FinanceFeeds, Nov 14).

Sunday night: Japan prelim GDP 6:50pm CT (fcst +0.1% q/q) and China Oct activity 8:00pm CT (retail sales +0.8% y/y, industrial output +5.3% y/y) — the first prints of the week before Canada CPI Mon 7:30am CT (Capital Street FX week-ahead).

Trump-Xi-Putin Shenzhen meeting has no agenda or format yet — Xi wary of hosting, US official says Trump unlikely to raise Ukraine; nuclear talks a nonstarter for Beijing; a meeting is still expected at APEC (Reuters, Nov 14).

CORRECTION: CFTC Nov 10 COT was NOT released Fri — the CFTC's own report page still shows Nov 3 positions as of Sat 14:35 CT, and no secondary summary exists. Veterans Day (Wed Nov 11) fell between the Tue as-of date and Fri, which under the CFTC holiday rule pushes the release to Mon Nov 16, 3:30pm ET. Nov 3 read stands: EUR net-short -157,791, JPY net-long +102,321.

Jefferson: taking his policy cues from inflation — 'the trajectory of inflation as providing the more important signal' — suggests he may support further hikes, but gives no pace guidance; joined the 10-2 Oct hold majority.

Dollar closes at a fresh 19-month high — DXY 103.41 (+0.24%); EUR/USD $1.1027 (-0.31%, lowest since Apr 2025), GBP/USD $1.3215, USD/JPY 159.79 after touching 160.19 in Tokyo; 10Y 5.15%, biggest weekly rise in 19 months.
items.source: The Trade Signal Fri close brief; Market Briefer

items.headline: Oil settles mixed — Brent $95.84 (+$0.02), WTI $88.56 (-0.20%) — both -2.5% on the week after the IEA surplus call (Q4 supply 105 mb/d, 1.7 mb/d above demand); US crude output hits a record 14.013 mb/d.

NZD gives back the election week — NZD/USD $0.5524 Fri close (-0.39%); Monday's post-election rise fully reversed. Preliminary count stands (National 42 seats, coalition 67/131 provisional); official result Nov 27.

Trump to meet Xi and Putin in Shenzhen on Thu Nov 19 — nuclear arms reductions and the US-Israeli war against Iran on the agenda, per the White House (Reuters); no agreement expected, per a senior US official. Scheduled meeting, flag for Monday.

Israel's security cabinet meets Sunday after instructing the IDF to raise readiness for a possible new strike on Iran (JFeed) — scheduled meeting, flag for Monday's runs; no new in-window development overnight, CENTCOM's Bahrain-radar denial stands.

PPI core read corrected: the standard core (ex-food-and-energy) printed +0.3% m/m, +5.0% y/y — exactly in line; the +0.5% was the trade-inclusive core (less foods, energy, trade). Post-print FedWatch 25bp 88.2% / 50bp 11.8% (CME).
Daly: 'rate increases likely' as inflation worsens — bias is further tightening, inflation 'bleeding' into services; rising yields 'most welcome', giving the Fed 'a little more time' (Reuters).
Bowman: core PCE seen at 3.3% in Oct; wants the AI and Middle East shocks to dissipate before believing inflation falls next year (FXStreet).
Collins: higher productivity has helped limit some inflation pressures; Logan: Treasury market functions 'very well' (squawk).
BofA adds a January 2027 hike to its Fed forecast and a third hike by March 2027; STIR ~28bp priced for December (squawk).
IEA: global oil market returns to surplus in Q4 for the first time since the Iran war — supply 105 mb/d, 1.7 mb/d above demand; Brent ~$95.7, WTI ~$88.4 after Thu's +$3.06 settle jump (IEA; Reuters).
Eurozone Q3 GDP 2nd estimate +0.4% q/q, unrevised from the Oct 30 flash; +1.3% y/y; employment flat — no EUR reaction, EUR/USD ~$1.1065 (Eurostat; Reuters).
